newsitem.title: UK: NNPC says won't decouple Qua, Bonny Light pricing.
newsitem.headline: NNPC says won't decouple Qua, Bonny Light pricing.

text.p: Nigeria on Wednesday said it would continue to issue a single price for sales of its Bonny Light and Qua Iboe crudes despite pressure from some buyers for state National Nigerian Petroleum Corp (NNPC) to set separate prices for the grades.
"NNPC is aware of a campaign by some buyers and traders to decouple Qua Iboe from Bonny Light," said a senior NNPC official.
"Existing NNPC policy was confirmed today by the honourable (oil) minister. Qua Iboe and Bonny Light will continue to be priced as a single unit. We have no intention of decoupling the prices."
Qua Iboe has been trading in recent weeks at a 5-10 cent discount to Bonny Light, traders said.
They said a preference among Asian buyers for Bonny Light combined with growing competition from Latin American grades for Qua Iboe in U.S. markets was probably behind the change.
The NNPC official said indications from the companies that produce Qua Iboe and Bonny Light were that market differences over the past two months between the grades were temporary.
Royal Dutch/Shell produces Bonny Light and Mobil Corp runs the Qua Iboe system.
NNPC said it had not ruled out the possibility of changing policy if a gap between prices persisted.
"If we find this to be a long term development we will respond but we are not yet convinced," said the NNPC official.
Nigeria sells some 900,000 barrels per day (bpd) of crude through about 30 contracts with traders and refiners, issuing prices each month according to NNPC's assessment of the spot crude market.
Total exports of around 1.8 million bpd also include liftings from joint venture partners.
